purpose: Assess ASVS V14 Data Protection, where almost every control that exists was built without a rule saying what it should protect.
requiredInvariants: A coverage claim names the denominator it measured, and pairs it with the negative check that makes it conclusive.
A framework directive is not a response header; force-dynamic and revalidate are never counted as anti-caching coverage.
Masking in logs is not masking in responses, and neither is minimization during processing.
A FAIL must name where the gap is; a missing control elsewhere is not evidence that a given endpoint over-returns.
A keyword match that turns out to classify code provenance rather than data is named as such, not silently dropped.
Evidence that lives outside the repository is NOT_ASSESSED, never FAIL, consistently with V4, V11, V12 and V16.
FAIL is recorded and reported, never resolved by editing product logic.
No product logic, dependency, production, REG.RU, DNS or database change.
acceptance: V14.3.2 states all 118 handlers and the full split (86 / 1 / 4 / 27), and says why the 4 framework-directive handlers are not coverage.
V14.2.3 establishes that the root layout reaches the authenticated surface by checking the nested layouts, rather than assuming it.
V14.2.4 names the Sentry filter's exact limits instead of calling it insufficient.
V14.2.6 is NOT_ASSESSED, not FAIL, because no over-returning endpoint was identified — an unearned FAIL is the same error as an unearned PASS.
V14.1.1 names the IP provenance documents that match a classification search and says why they are not one.
V14.2.7 credits both retention mechanisms that exist before recording the gap.
V14.3.3 credits the machine-checked absence of credentials in browser storage before recording the personal data that is there.
All 13 V14 requirements are decided: 0 PASS, 10 FAIL, 3 not assessed — and the zero is reported plainly.
